# Metrics and health

With `--metrics-listen 127.0.0.1:9233` the kernel serves plain HTTP with no login on that address, so bind it to a private one. How to use it for health checks, alerts and graphs: [Monitor kernable](../how-to/monitor).

- `GET /metrics`: Prometheus text format, below.
- `GET /health`: 200 while the process runs.
- `GET /ready`: 200 once every aggregate that counts has a worker connected and every listener that counts is connected and has caught up (see [Who counts](../concepts/ordering#who-counts)), else 503 naming the workers or listeners it waits for.

Counters and durations count since the kernel started and begin at 0 again after a restart. Durations are summaries without quantiles, in seconds: `<name>_sum` and `<name>_count`. The `outcome` label takes the values named in the description; the `listener` label is a listener's name, for every registered listener, connected or not.

| Metric | Type | Labels | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kernable_commands_total` | counter | `outcome` | Commands completed since the kernel started, by outcome: committed, or rejected by a worker or the kernel (scheduled commands cancelled, expired, or refused by a middleware when due included). Commands a middleware refused before the queue are not counted. |
| `kernable_queries_total` | counter | `outcome` | Queries since the kernel started, by outcome: answered; rejected by a read model or a middleware; failed when no read model answered, because none was connected or none answered in time. |
| `kernable_middleware_total` | counter | `outcome`, `reason` | Runs of a middleware chain, before or after a command or query, by outcome: passed, rejected, or failed when a middleware in the chain was not connected or did not answer within --middleware-timeout-ms. |
| `kernable_refused_total` | counter |  | Requests and connections a limit refused since the kernel started, by reason: connections, requests_per_key, rate, quota_storage, subscriptions_per_key, listeners_per_key, queued_commands, queued_per_aggregate, queued_bytes, cache_bytes, handshake_timeout, too_large, http_host, http_connections. |
| `kernable_queued_commands` | gauge |  | Commands stored in the queue and not completed yet: waiting for a worker or running. |
| `kernable_scheduled_commands` | gauge |  | Scheduled commands (deliver_at) not due yet, or due and being checked before they join their aggregate's queue; counted in kernable_queued_commands too. |
| `kernable_worker_sessions` | gauge |  | Worker sessions connected now. |
| `kernable_head_position` | gauge |  | Global position of the newest stored event; 0 while the store is empty. |
| `kernable_execution_seconds` | summary |  | Seconds from handing a command to a worker until its events are committed: the worker round trip plus storage. Committed commands only. |
| `kernable_settle_seconds` | summary |  | Seconds from the commit until every listener that counts acknowledged the events. Settling submits that settled in time only. |
| `kernable_query_seconds` | summary |  | Seconds from handing a query to the read models until one answered or rejected it. Queries that failed are not included. |
| `kernable_middleware_seconds` | summary |  | Seconds one middleware chain took to pass, reject or fail a request. |
| `kernable_listener_position` | gauge | `listener` | Global position of the last event the listener acknowledged. |
| `kernable_listener_lag` | gauge | `listener` | Global positions between the newest stored event and the listener's position: how far it is behind. |
| `kernable_listener_connected` | gauge | `listener` | 1 while the listener is connected, 0 while it is registered but away. |
| `kernable_listener_parked` | gauge |  | Events the listener gave up on and parked, waiting for an operator to retry or dismiss them. |
| `kernable_listener_skipped` | gauge |  | Events the listener skipped since the kernel started because its code does not know them (a newer schema): its deployment is older than the events. |
| `kernable_record_head` | gauge |  | The newest record of the record log a standby follows (--replication sync). |
| `kernable_standby_acknowledged` | gauge |  | The newest record the standby holds on its disk; writes after it wait. |
| `kernable_standby_in_sync` | gauge |  | 1 while a standby is connected and has caught up; without it, writes wait. |
| `kernable_standby_catching_up` | gauge |  | 1 while no standby has caught up yet (without a witness): writes are told without one. |
| `kernable_store_bytes` | gauge |  | Bytes the event store, the vault and the files take on the disk, measured every 10 s. |
| `kernable_store_bytes_max` | gauge |  | --max-store-bytes: at it, new commands and file puts are refused (quota_storage). |
| `kernable_ready` | gauge |  | 1 while the kernel is ready: every aggregate that counts has a worker, every listener that counts is connected and caught up, and it is not shutting down. |
| `kernable_standby_applied` | gauge |  | On a standby: the newest record of the primary's log it holds. |
| `kernable_standby_lag` | gauge |  | On a standby: records it is behind the primary's head as last seen. |
| `kernable_process_cases` | gauge | `process`, `state` | Cases per process and state: running (a command sent or a query asked), waiting (for an event or a time), incident (stopped until an operator resolves it) held now; ended since the kernel started. |
| `kernable_process_incidents` | counter | `process` | Incidents raised since the kernel started, per process. |
| `kernable_process_step_seconds` | histogram | `process`, `step` | Seconds from reaching a step until it completed, per process and step. |

## kernable node

With `metrics-listen` in its `[node]` section, `kernable node` serves `GET /metrics` too, a line per child (the kernel, the backup follower, each service), named by the `child` label ([Run a node from one file](../how-to/node#metrics)).

| Metric | Type | Labels | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kernable_node_child_up` | gauge | `child` | Whether the child runs (1) or not (0). |
| `kernable_node_child_restarts_total` | counter | `child` | Times the node started the child again. |
| `kernable_node_child_uptime_seconds` | gauge | `child` | Seconds since the child last started, while it runs. |
| `kernable_node_container_cpu_seconds_total` | counter | `child` | CPU time a child's container used (a service, and on Linux the kernel and the backup follower), from its cgroup. |
| `kernable_node_container_memory_bytes` | gauge | `child` | Memory a child's container uses now, from its cgroup. |
